title.en: Risk briefing for a mountain trip
title.es: Charla de riesgos para una excursión

es: Presentar en una charla breve los riesgos de una excursión (peligro, probabilidad, consecuencia y medida de prevención) y deducir las causas de un incidente con must have, might have y can't have.

teaching.en: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the measure we take.
teaching.es: Esta charla tiene tres partes: el peligro, el riesgo y la medida que tomamos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una charla de riesgos sigue un orden fijo: peligro, riesgo (probabilidad) y medida.
segments: This briefing has three parts: the hazard,
the risk and the measure we take.
teaching.audioText: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the measure we take.

teaching.en: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious injury.
teaching.es: Es probable que haya hielo en la cresta, y la consecuencia podría ser una lesión grave.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de la probabilidad se nombra la consecuencia: could be + lo que podría pasar.
segments: Ice is likely on the ridge, and
the consequence could be a serious injury.
teaching.audioText: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious injury.

teaching.en: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment.
teaching.es: Para evitar una caída, todos los participantes deben revisar su equipo.
teaching.explanationEs: To prevent + nombre abre la medida; must marca la obligación.
teaching.audioText: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment.

teaching.en: The path is wet, so the incident must have happened after the rain.
teaching.es: El camino está mojado, así que el incidente debe de haber ocurrido después de la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado, a partir de una prueba.
segments: The path is wet, so the incident
must have happened after the rain.
teaching.audioText: The path is wet, so the incident must have happened after the rain.

teaching.en: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm.
teaching.es: No hay indicios de daños por el viento, así que la causa no puede haber sido la tormenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: deducción negativa casi segura.
segments: There is no evidence of wind damage, so
the cause can't have been the storm.
teaching.audioText: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm.

teaching.en: The incident might have started with a missed turn.
teaching.es: El incidente podría haber empezado con un giro que no se tomó.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad sobre el pasado, sin seguridad.
teaching.audioText: The incident might have started with a missed turn.

hint.es: La frase empieza con To prevent y acaba con la medida.

feedback.es: Con una prueba fuerte, must have + participio expresa la deducción casi segura; can't have la descartaría y must leave no habla del pasado.

hint.es: La prueba es fuerte: busca must have + participio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué medida se pide para evitar una lesión.

choices.text: Crossing the river as fast as possible.
Crossing the river one person at a time.

feedback.es: La medida contra las caídas en el río es cruzar de uno en uno y revisar el equipo.

origin.audio: Good morning. The main hazard today is the river. The consequence could be an injury if someone falls, so participants must cross one at a time and check their equipment.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La causa podría haber sido un mapa viejo.»

answer.text: The cause might have been an old map

feedback.es: Might have been + nombre expresa una posibilidad sobre la causa de algo ya ocurrido.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que resume bien el pronóstico.

choices.text: It will probably rain, and a storm is highly likely.
It might rain, and a storm will definitely come.
It will definitely rain, but a storm is unlikely.

feedback.es: Lluvia casi segura se dice will definitely rain; una tormenta muy improbable, unlikely.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consejo da el parte.

choices.text: To leave the ridge before two.
To start the climb at three.

feedback.es: El parte aconseja estar fuera de la cresta antes de las dos, porque las tormentas son posibles después de las tres.

origin.audio: Mountain report. Thunderstorms are possible after three. You had better be off the ridge by two, and carry a torch in case you come down late.

prompt.es: Completa: «No salgas a menos que el viento haya bajado.»

feedback.es: Unless significa «si no»: solo salgas si el viento ha bajado.

origin.text: Don't set off ___ the wind has dropped.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de una charla de riesgos para una excursión.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must wear strong boots, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. Finally, check your equipment now, so that nothing breaks on the way. Are there any questions?
accepted: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must wear strong boots, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. Finally, check your equipment now, so that nothing breaks on the way. Are there any questions?

Hello, team. Today I want to explain two risks. The main hazard is the wind on the high ground. Strong gusts are very likely, and the consequence could be a fall or another injury. To prevent it, we will stay on the marked route, and you had better hold your hats. The other hazard is the cold. The odds are that it will freeze tonight, so everybody must bring a warm coat, provided that there is space in the bag. In case anyone feels dizzy, tell me at once. Unless the forecast improves, we will not climb the summit. Does everyone understand?

feedback.es: Una charla clara nombra cada peligro, dice cuán probable es, avisa de la consecuencia y cierra con una medida de prevención (to prevent, unless, in case, so that, had better).

origin.text: Vas a dirigir la charla de riesgos de una excursión de un día con un sendero de montaña, una cresta y un río. Escribe el guion (entre 100 y 180 palabras): dos peligros con su probabilidad, su consecuencia y una medida de prevención (to prevent, so that, unless, in case o had better).

prompt.es: Elige el aviso correcto para un accidente poco probable.

choices.text: In the unlikely event of an accident is, call the guide.
In the unlikely event of an accident, call the guide.
The odds are against to call the guide.

feedback.es: Event of lleva un nombre (an accident); las otras opciones mezclan estructuras o construyen mal la frase.

origin.text: You tell your group that an accident is very unlikely, and you give an instruction in case it happens.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deduce el hablante.

feedback.es: El hablante deduce con must have que alguien se fue con prisa y, como no hay indicios de un accidente, descarta una emergencia.

origin.audio: I found the tent open and the boots gone. Somebody must have left in a hurry, but there is no evidence of an accident, so it can't have been an emergency.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase con so that sobre un mapa y una persona que no se pierde.

answer.text: We check the map so that nobody gets lost.

We are checking the map so that nobody gets lost.
Check the map so that nobody gets lost.
We check the map so that no one gets lost.
We check the map so nobody gets lost.

We always check the map so that nobody gets lost.

feedback.es: So that + oración en presente expresa la finalidad de una medida preventiva.

origin.text: Escribe una frase en inglés: revisamos el mapa para que nadie se pierda.
